title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Azerbaijani Who Moved Abroad. Tip #1
body: He left for Turkey, Germany, Poland, or Canada, and he now begins sentences with "in Europe" the way other people clear their throat. Ask how long he's been gone. Under a year and he still defends Baku. Over three and he criticises it constantly and would move back tomorrow if anyone offered him a reason. Both are homesickness. It's a sealed deal if he has explained the Azerbaijani tea ceremony to a foreigner more than ten times.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 xaricdə yaşayanlar, come get your people.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Azerbaijani Who Moved Abroad. Tip #2
body: Watch the airport arrival, because it is a whole production. Eleven relatives came. Somebody is holding flowers. The suitcase is entirely gifts and it was weighed three times at the other end. He is exhausted and being asked questions before he's out of the car park. It's a sealed deal if a cousin he has not spoken to in four years is at the airport and hugs him first.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Azerbaijani Who Moved Abroad. Tip #3
body: Ask what he brought back. Chocolate, perfume, and something electronic, and there is a list, and his mother made it, and it was updated by voice note over six weeks. Somebody asked for a specific item they saw online and would not be talked out of it. It's a sealed deal if he's ever paid excess baggage on things he did not want and could not refuse.

Tip #3 😭 xaricdə yaşayanlar, come get your people.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Azerbaijani Who Moved Abroad. Tip #4
body: Ask what he misses and see how fast the answer comes. It is never the country in the abstract. It is a specific thing: his mother's dolma, a tea house, one street in the evening, the way the Boulevard smells in September. Nobody misses a nation. Everyone misses a Tuesday. It's a sealed deal if he goes quiet for a second before answering.

Tip #4 😭 xaricdə yaşayanlar, come get your people.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Azerbaijani Who Moved Abroad. Tip #5
body: Watch the first week back. Everything is smaller than he remembered and he says so out loud, once, and a relative takes it badly. He complains about the driving. He complains about the service. Then day five arrives, he sees somebody, and he stops complaining entirely. It's a sealed deal if he has said "I could actually live here again" on day six and unsaid it by day ten.

Tip #5 😭 xaricdə yaşayanlar, come get your people.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Azerbaijani Who Moved Abroad. Tip #6
body: Ask about the money. He sends some home and he does not discuss it, ever, with anyone, because that's the arrangement. The family knows and does not mention it either. There is an entire economy running on this silence. It's a sealed deal if the amount goes up every year and nobody has ever named a figure out loud.
caption:
Tip #6 😭 xaricdə yaşayanlar, come get your people.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot an Azerbaijani Who Moved Abroad. Tip #7
body: Ask about the passport and the plan, because there is always a plan, with a year attached. Residency at this point, citizenship at that point, then bring the parents, then decide. He has run the timeline so many times he no longer needs to think. It's a sealed deal if he can tell you the exact number of days he still needs to be in the country.
